QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member)` renames each member for outside code... the default expansion is `private_##member`, so `ssl->MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(conf)` becomes `ssl->private_conf`. An application that touches `ssl->conf` directly therefore fails to compile instead of silently depending on the layout.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that opacity is enforced at compile time by renaming the member to `private_<name>`, so direct access fails to compile. The struct stays in the public headers. It does not say the layout is hidden, and the fields remain visible by implication.
